title: Pioneer Genomics On-prem / Air-gapped Deployment Discovery
summary: Discovery focused on Pioneer Genomics' regulatory need for an air-gapped on-prem deployment. Key topics: offline model updates, hardware constraints (NVIDIA A100 vs H100/cost), FIPS/KMS/HSM integration, SOC2/ISO audit evidence, network isolation, deployment automation (airgap update process), expected throughput & latency SLOs, pilot scope and next steps. Action: Redwood to send security whitepaper, draft pilot plan, propose HW sizing options and benchmark plan.

transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-04-04T15:00Z - Duration 52 minutes
Attendees: Alec Rivers (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Chen (CTO, Pioneer), Raj Patel (Infra Lead), Lena Ortiz (CISO), Tomás Ruiz (ML Platform), Susan Lee (Compliance)

00:00 Alec: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this focused - I'm Alec from Redwood inference, joining me are Priya and Jordan from engineering. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Maya: Good, thanks. Appreciate you making time. We're trying to figure out how to run LLM inference on-prem in an air-gapped environment for our clinical genomics workloads.
00:14 Alec: Great, can you give us the top constraints? Compliance, hardware, that sort of thing.
00:19 Maya: Sure - number one is regulatory: we cannot send PHI or genomic sequences offsite. So hosted API is out. We need a private deployment inside our data center with full network isolation - basically air-gapped.
00:29 Raj: To add, our data center policy disallows outbound internet from the inference tier; updates go through an approval channel and are applied manually - so any vendor solution needs an offline update path.
00:38 Priya: OK, thanks. When you say offline updates, do you mean full model images are shipped on media or you run a package signed artifact that we import? How do you currently handle OS/security patches?
00:47 Raj: We use signed packages and an internal update appliance that verifies signatures. For models, we prefer vendor-signed tarballs that we can hash verify.
00:56 Jordan: Redwood supports air-gapped installs - we provide an appliance image and signed model artifacts plus an update bundle. There was a note about per-customer key signing for artifacts - is that a hard requirement?
01:05 Lena: Preferably yes. We want to be able to verify vendor provenance with our own root-of-trust (we use an internal CA). Also HSM-backed signing and key rotation policy is part of our audit.
01:14 Priya: We can accommodate HSM KMS integrations; our private deploy supports customer-managed KMS endpoints and we can plug into your HSM by key import or remote HSM integration - depending on policy. We do need to understand if FIPS 140-2/3 is required for you.
01:25 Susan: FIPS validated crypto is required for a subset of workloads. We'll need evidence. Also SOC2 and ISO artifacts are standard ask.
01:33 Alec: We'll send our SOC2 report, ISO statement, and a short whitepaper on the air-gapped install flow.
01:37 Tomás: On the compute side - what GPU profiles do you support? We currently have a mix of A100 40GB and a few H100s but not many. Price/perf will matter; quantized models could help.
01:47 Priya: We optimize for A100 and H100, and we have quantized model variants for INT8/FP16 paths. Important to note: latency and throughput vary with quantization and KV cache sizes. What's your expected SLOs and typical sequence length?
01:58 Tomás: For our clinical inference pipeline it's mostly short sequences, like 128-512 tokens, but we sometimes have longer context for reports up to 2k tokens. Latency SLO ~ 200-500 ms per request for short prompts, throughput about 60 reqs/sec sustained with bursts to 150.
02:14 Priya: That gives us a ballpark. For 60 qps with 128 tokens and an A100 80GB you'd likely need N instances depending on batching - we can propose a sizing matrix. Also, batching helps cost but might add tail latency; with continuous batching we can keep p99 in range but we need traces.
02:27 Raj: We'll share traces. However, our network fabric between GPUs is older; NVLink is limited on some racks. Any recommendations?
02:34 Jordan: For multi-GPU models or partitioned KV caches, NVLink benefits are significant. If NVLink isn't available, we can route to single-GPU model variants or use model sharding with extra latency cost. We'll detail tradeoffs in the pilot.
02:44 Maya: Updates - what's the step for model updates? We can't allow the inference infra to pull from external repos.
02:50 Priya: Standard flow: Redwood provides a signed model bundle, you verify via your CA/HSM, then an offline install service imports the bundle to the private control plane. We also produce a delta update path so you don't always ship a full 30-50GB image - diffs can be applied offline.
03:06 Lena: Deltas are better but how do you guarantee determinism? We need reproducible builds and an audit trail.
03:11 Jordan: Our build system can produce reproducible artifacts with checksums and a manifest. We log a full install audit and provide signed attestations for each install event - logs include commit hashes and kernel/driver versions.
03:22 Raj: Speaking of drivers, we run RHEL with a locked kernel, and driver updates go through change control. We'll need a compatibility matrix for driver/kernel combos.
03:30 Priya: We'll provide a tested matrix for recommended driver versions and a checklist to validate before installation.
03:33 Tomás: For model performance, can you run an on-prem microbench with our workload?
03:37 Priya: Yes - our pilot normally includes a benchmark agent you run locally against our inference runtime. We can adapt the script to your traces and run in air-gapped mode; results produce latency, p99, tokens/sec, and token cost estimates.
03:47 Maya: Good. Compliance question: Do you support local logging only, or does Redwood expect telemetry outbound?
03:52 Alec: For private installs, telemetry is optional. We can run fully offline with logs stored locally. For troubleshooting, customers can choose to share telemetry artifacts manually.
03:59 Lena: And SSO? We use SAML with an internal IdP and RBAC mapped to AD groups.
04:04 Priya: Private control plane integrates with SAML/SO and LDAP; role mappings can be configured.
04:09 Susan: Audit logs retention policy - what granularity and retention windows are supported?
04:13 Jordan: We capture request logs at token granularity if enabled, plus admin actions. Retention is configurable; we can support your retention policy but storage sizing has to be planned.
04:21 Raj: Network isolation - is there any component that must be internet reachable for licensing or attestation?
04:26 Alec: No. For air-gapped, license verification is offline via signed entitlements. Remote attestation can be optional; we support hardware attestation flows if you enable an internal verifier.
04:35 Tomás: Any known gotchas for GPUs older than A100? We have a couple V100s in cold racks.
04:40 Priya: V100 is supported but performance per watt is lower; also some newer attention kernels are optimized for Ampere/Blackwell. For heavy throughput we recommend A100/H100. We'll show delta in the sizing doc.
04:52 Maya: Pricing - are you doing committed dedicated capacity or a perpetual license for private?
04:56 Alec: For private on-prem we have enterprise licensing: a platform fee plus support tier; optional reserved capacity pricing if we provide managed hardware. We'll share a pricing matrix.
05:04 Maya: Timeline - we'd like to pilot within 4-6 weeks. Is that realistic?
05:08 Priya: Yes, if we get your GPU inventory and sample traces this week we can scope a 2-week bench + 2-week pilot. We'll need PO and network access windows for on-site install, if required.
05:18 Alec: Let's recap next steps quickly. We'll send SOC2 artifacts and the air-gapped whitepaper, Priya will draft pilot plan + sizing, and you (Raj/Tomás) will share traces and GPU inventory. We'll schedule workshop for wk of Apr 20.
05:28 Maya: Sounds good. One last question - have you done HIPAA customers?
05:32 Alec: Yes, we have customers in healthcare; we can share redacted references and compliance attestations.
05:36 Susan: We'll want to see a sample runbook and incident response playbook as well.
05:40 Alec: We'll include that in the package to you.
05:42 Maya: Great, thanks everyone.
05:44 Alec: Thanks, we'll follow up with the materials.
05:47 (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: minor mis-transcriptions around KV cache spelled 'K V cash' in the automated diffusion; some speaker attribution shifts around 02:00-02:30 but content verified by AE.
notes: Recorded in PST time; customer is highly regulated (PHI/genomic data). They require offline update bundles, HSM/KMS integration, FIPS crypto for subset of workloads, and an audit trail. Pilot requested: run adapted benchmark in air-gapped mode, propose hardware options (A100/H100), provide SOC2/ISO artifacts, runbook, and compliance docs.
